statement: The function returns a result r such that: (a) there exists i with 0 <= i < len(nums), nums[i] = target, and r = abs(i - start); and (b) for every j with 0 <= j < len(nums) and nums[j] = target, r <= abs(j - start). Equivalently, r is the minimum of abs(i - start) over all indices i with nums[i] = target.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 10000; 0 <= start < len(nums); there exists k with 0 <= k < len(nums) and nums[k] = target.

statement: Whenever get_min_distance(nums, target, start) returns a result r and get_min_distance(nums', target, start) returns a result r', we have r = r'.

Whenever get_min_distance(nums, target, start) returns a result r and get_min_distance(nums_rev, target, start_rev) returns a result r', we have r = r'.

statement: Whenever get_min_distance(nums, target, start) returns a result r and nums[start] != target, r is the minimum of the nonempty set { start - i | 0 <= i < start and nums[i] = target } union { i - start | start < i < len(nums) and nums[i] = target }.
